Partially. The EFI image carries the Microsoft+Canonical dual-signed shim and Canonical-signed GRUB, so the boot menu loads and renders. Fix: Bring the backend up, point the proxy at the right port, or raise proxy timeouts. The nginx error log names the failing upstream and the reason.

From the Universe OS MEMORY.md: explain Deadliest traps.

- `/etc/polkit-1/rules.d` must be **0755** or rules are invisible; the sync script restores a setuid/setgid mode table. Every new pkexec'd helper must be in the `49-universe.rules` allowlist. `AUTH_SELF_KEEP` forces a password even for policy-`yes` → `org.freedesktop.accounts.` = `NOT_HANDLED`. **`pkexec` refuses from the serial console** (its session is never "active", so it falls to password auth and the console hangs at `Password:` - escape with a raw Ctrl-C). To drive the live session from the console, go under the session bus directly: `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=unix:path=/run/user/1000/bus gsettings …`. - rsync: `--keep-dirlinks` mandatory; never `--delete` (orphans stay in the chroot — delete by hand); never plain `-a` as non-root. Recompile both dconf dbs. - **Build the ISO as the NORMAL user — that is what `build-iso-noroot.sh` means.** Run unprivileged, mksquashfs silently skips root-only (0700) entries, and that is exactly what keeps chroot test junk (`/tmp/cprof*` browser profiles, `/root/.cache`, `/root/.pki`) out of the image; `sudo bash build-iso-noroot.sh` packs all of it — one sudo build came out 135 MB fatter than the same content built as kali. `etc/polkit-1` and `build/image` are kali-owned precisely so the build works without root. The sync script is the one that needs sudo. The build also purges `$CH/tmp` (minus `.X11-unix`) as belt-and-braces for kali-owne

Sources live in `scripts/chrome-theme/` (`newtab.html` + `deck.js` + `page.css` + `content.js`); the same deck is also the browser's `file://` home page. - **`--load-extension` no longer works** (Chrome 137+). The only way to ship a theme is a signed CRX3 advertised through `/usr/share/google-chrome/extensions/<id>.json` (`{"external_crx": ..., "external_version": ...}`). CRX3 = `Cr24` + u32(3) + u32(header_len) + protobuf header + zip, signed over `b"CRX3 SignedData\x00" + u32(len(signed_header_data)) + signed_header_data + zip`. From the Universe OS MEMORY.md: explain Shell, dock, icons, dconf (v0.3.7).

- **A single bad group name kills the whole dconf database.** In a dconf keyfile, `[org/gnome/terminal/legacy/profiles:/]` produces the path `.../profiles://default` and `dconf compile` rejects the *entire file*, not just that key — so nothing from the system db applied. The correct group is `[org/gnome/terminal/legacy/profiles:]` (no trailing slash); the per-profile one keeps it: `[.../profiles:/:universe]`. The sync script hard-fails if those four links are missing. 3. `rsync` must never run with `--delete` here: `scripts/rootfs` is an overlay on a full debootstrap system; `--delete` wipes the base. 4. `set -e` + `st=$?` on the next line = dead code: the failed command closes the shell right there, so the fallback never runs.
